skill.name: ai-video-generation
skill.description: Guides users through generating and processing AI videos with the inference.sh infsh CLI. Covers text-to-video, image-to-video, avatar lipsync, upscaling, foley, and clip merging across supported model apps.
skill.summary: Generate and process AI video workflows with the inference.sh CLI.
skill.author: skillssh

security_audit.summary: Static Ruby/shell backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code and fenced command examples. Hardcoded URL findings are documentation links or placeholder media URLs, not hidden network calls. The skill has medium contextual risk because it grants broad infsh CLI access and sends prompts or media URLs to external video services.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the smallest set of infsh commands needed, or require explicit user confirmation before running generation, login, listing, or media-processing commands.
Warn users that prompts and image, audio, or video URLs may be sent to inference.sh and downstream model providers. Recommend non-sensitive assets or expiring URLs.
Label example URLs as user-provided placeholders and avoid suggesting public links for private media workflows.

semantic_findings.title: Broad CLI Permission for External Service
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares allowed-tools: Bash(infsh *), which lets the agent run any infsh subcommand. Since infsh communicates with external video services, prompts and media references may leave the user environment or incur usage costs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit, and the skill documents infsh app run workflows throughout SKILL.md. The risk is contextual rather than evidence of malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: External Media Processing Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The examples ask users to provide image, audio, and video URLs for avatar, lipsync, upscaling, foley, and merging workflows. Private or signed media URLs could be exposed to inference.sh or model providers during normal use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple documented examples include media URL inputs sent to remote model apps. This is expected functionality, but it creates a privacy and data-handling risk for sensitive media.

content.value_statement: Creating AI video workflows often requires matching each task to a model and command pattern. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh video generation, animation, lipsync, and utility workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides text-to-video generation with app IDs such as Google Veo and Grok Imagine Video.
Supports image-to-video workflows using Wan, Seedance, and P-Video model references.
Provides avatar animation and lipsync examples for OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse.
Shows video utility workflows for upscaling, foley sound, and media merging.
Lists related skills and documentation links for broader inference.sh media pipelines.
limitations: Requires a configured inference.sh account and the infsh CLI.
Model availability, cost, duration, and output quality depend on inference.sh and provider limits.
Prompts and media URLs may be processed by external services.
Does not handle rights clearance, brand review, or final video editing decisions.

use_cases.title: Create Social Media Clips
use_cases.description: Generate short promotional or story-driven clips from text prompts and simple creative direction.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Videos
use_cases.description: Compare model choices for product teasers, explainer clips, and first-frame controlled animation.

use_cases.title: Build Media Automation Pipelines
use_cases.description: Combine generation, foley, upscaling, and merging steps into repeatable CLI-driven workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Video Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a five-second AI video about [topic]. Recommend a suitable inference.sh video model and draft a concise generation prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Source Image
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an image URL: [image URL]. Choose an image-to-video model and describe the motion, camera movement, and expected input fields.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Avatar Clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an avatar video using a portrait URL and narration audio URL. Select an appropriate model and list the inputs I should confirm before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Step Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an inference.sh workflow that generates a clip, adds foley sound, upscales the result, and merges it with another clip. Include review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A marketer wants a short launch video for a new mobile app.
output: Recommended a fast text-to-video model for early concept review.
Drafted a prompt with product context, camera direction, and duration guidance.
Suggested upscaling only after the concept clip is approved.

output_examples.input: A creator has a product image and wants a smooth animated reveal.
output: Selected an image-to-video workflow instead of pure text-to-video.
Defined motion direction, framing, and visual constraints for the source image.
Flagged that the image URL should not expose private or sensitive assets.

output_examples.input: A developer needs a repeatable video pipeline for campaign assets.
output: Outlined generation, sound, upscaling, and merging stages.
Separated creative review points from automated processing steps.
Identified external-service and media-privacy checks before execution.

best_practices: Confirm model choice, cost, duration, and media inputs before running infsh commands.
Use non-sensitive assets or expiring URLs when sending media to external services.
Start with short drafts, review results, then upscale or merge approved clips.
anti_patterns: Do not send private customer media without permission and provider review.
Do not run broad generation workflows before confirming the target model and expected cost.
Do not rely on generated clips as final brand assets without human review.

faq.question: What CLI does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the inference.sh infsh CLI to run hosted video and media-processing apps.

faq.question: Can it generate video from text?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes text-to-video examples for models such as Google Veo and Grok Imagine Video.

faq.question: Can it animate an existing image?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents image-to-video workflows for models such as Wan, Seedance, and P-Video.

faq.question: Does it support avatar or lipsync video?
faq.answer: Yes. It references OmniHuman, Fabric, and PixVerse workflows for avatar and lipsync use cases.

faq.question: Are external services involved?
faq.answer: Yes. Prompts and media URLs may be sent to inference.sh and downstream model providers during normal use.

faq.question: Do users need an account?
faq.answer: Users need the infsh CLI installed and an inference.sh account configured before generation commands can run.
